newsitem.title: BERMUDA: RTRS-Canada's Martin says deal on IMF gold sale close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canada's Martin says deal on IMF gold sale close.

text.p: Agreement is getting close to sell IMF gold to help finance a bail-out for the world's poorest debtors is close, Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday.
But, in an interview with Reuters, he said he was not sure whether agreement could be reached at next week's annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington.
"I think consensus is reasonably close. I don't know if it will come out of Washington or not," he said.

"What is important is that those who oppose gold sales have the responsibility to come up with better alternatives...I don't know any better alternatives," said Martin, who is in Bermuda for a meeting of Commonwealth finance ministers.

Gold sales opponents include Germany and Italy but are supported by a number of other industrial nations, such as the U.S. and Britain which originally proposed the idea as a means to finance debt relief for the world's poorest countries.
Martin said only a small percentage of the IMF's $40 billion gold holdings would be sold and could in the future be replenished.
